facts.statement: Pseudhesperosuchus is a genus of sphenosuchian, which is a type of basal crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: Pseudhesperosuchus (meaning "false Hesperosuchus") is a genus of sphenosuchian, a type of basal crocodylomorph

facts.statement: The genus was named by José Bonaparte in 1969.
facts.quote: The genus was named by José Bonaparte in 1969

facts.statement: Recent redescription identified the type specimen as immature based on open neurocentral sutures on its cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: the holotype was recently redescribed in more detail, which identified the type specimen as inmature due to open neurocentral sutures on its cervical vertebra.

facts.statement: The skull is nearly complete but poorly preserved, with some bones misidentified and artificial holes created during preparation.
facts.quote: The skull, though nearly complete, is poorly preserved, some of its bones and sutures have been misidentified over the years, and additional artificial fenestrae made during preparation have been identified.

facts.statement: A 2002 study found Pseudhesperosuchus to have an unresolved phylogenetic position, neither closer to true crocodiles nor to Sphenosuchus.
facts.quote: A 2002 phylogenetic analysis of sphenosuchians performed by James Clark and Hans–Dieter Sues found Pseudhesperosuchus to have an unresolved position along with several other sphenosuchians, neither closer to true crocodiles or to Sphenosuchus.

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Norian stage, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The animal is known from a partial skeleton and skull found in the Late Triassic Los Colorados Formation of northwestern Argentina.
rejected.quote: It is known from a partial skeleton and skull found in rocks of the Late Triassic (Norian-age) Los Colorados Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina.
